introduction-the-wiki-rot-crisis.core: Wikis decay: pages are written once, never updated, duplicated and impossible to find, so developers stop trusting docs. Documentation engineering treats knowledge as a product: versioned with code, reviewed, searchable, measured for freshness and owned.

first_principles.problem: A developer follows a wiki runbook, the commands fail, and they never trust the wiki again.
truths: Unfindable docs might as well not exist.
derivation: Measure **freshness**; treat docs as a **platform product**.

analogy.title: A conference-room whiteboard
analogy.story: A useful diagram is drawn once, then partially erased and overwritten until nobody knows which parts are true.
analogy.breaks: Tools alone don't fix rot. Ownership and habits matter.

example.title: A trust collapse

steps.label: Lesson
steps.detail: Stale docs are worse than none.

example.outcome: you can see why docs need engineering.

check.q: Why are stale docs worse than no docs?
check.a: People follow them confidently, causing errors and delays, and then stop trusting all documentation.

docs-as-code-the-workflow.core: Docs-as-code uses developer tools for docs: Markdown in Git next to code, pull-request reviews, CI that builds, lints and link-checks, static-site generators (MkDocs, Docusaurus) and automatic publishing, so docs change in the same PR as the code they describe.

first_principles.problem: Code changes in PRs while the docs live in a separate wiki that nobody updates.
truths: Same-PR updates keep docs in sync.
CI catches broken links and formatting.
derivation: Have **CI** lint (Vale, markdownlint), check links, and build.

analogy.title: Writing the manual alongside the product design
analogy.story: When the design changes, the manual's change is in the same engineering change order.
analogy.breaks: Non-engineers may find Git hard, so provide editors or web UIs.

example.title: A docs CI job

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: Broken docs fail the build like broken code.

code.text:
- run: npx markdownlint-cli2 "docs/**/*.md"
- run: vale docs/
- run: lychee --no-progress docs/   # link checker
- run: mkdocs build --strict

example.outcome: docs kept in sync with the code.

check.q: What's the key benefit of updating docs in the same PR as code?
check.a: Docs stay synchronised with the code changes they describe and are reviewed together.

diagrams-as-code-mermaidjs.core: Diagrams as images (Visio, exported PNGs) can't be diffed, reviewed or easily updated. Diagrams-as-code (Mermaid, PlantUML, D2, Structurizr) write diagrams as text that lives in Git, renders automatically and changes in PRs.

first_principles.problem: An architecture PNG from 2021 is wrong, and nobody has the original Visio file to update it.
truths: Rendered diagrams can be generated anywhere.
derivation: Store them **next to the docs** in Git.
**Update in PRs** with the architecture change.

analogy.title: Sheet music vs. a recording
analogy.story: Sheet music can be edited note by note; a recording must be re-made from scratch.
analogy.breaks: Complex visual layouts can be hard to control in text, so use the right tool for the job.

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: Diagram changes are reviewed like code.

code.text:
sequenceDiagram
  Client->>API: POST /orders
  API->>DB: insert order
  API->>Queue: publish OrderCreated
  API-->>Client: 201 Created

check.q: Why are diagrams-as-code easier to keep current than image files?
check.a: They're text that can be edited, diffed and reviewed in PRs without the original design tool.

search-indexing-the-findability-problem.core: Docs nobody can find are useless. Invest in unified search across repos and sites (Algolia, Backstage search, Elastic), with good titles, metadata, a clear information architecture and analytics on failed searches.

first_principles.problem: 'I know it's documented somewhere' turns into 20 minutes of searching and a Slack question.
truths: Titles and metadata drive search quality.
derivation: Have **unified search** across all doc sources.
Design the **information architecture** (by task and audience).
**Track zero-result searches** and fill the gaps.

analogy.title: A library with a good catalogue
analogy.story: Without a catalogue, books are shelved randomly and might as well not exist.
analogy.breaks: Search can't fix bad content, so findability and quality go together.

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: Docs follow what users actually look for.

check.q: Why track zero-result searches in a documentation site?
check.a: They reveal topics users need that aren't documented or aren't findable.

measuring-freshness-the-stale-metrics.core: Measure doc freshness: last-updated dates, ownership, review intervals, broken-link counts, page feedback ('was this helpful?') and staleness relative to related code changes. Surface them so stale docs get fixed or archived.

first_principles.problem: Pages that say 'Last updated: 2019' erode trust, and nobody knows which ones are still accurate.
derivation: **Archive** unowned stale pages, with a clear banner.

analogy.title: Expiry dates on food
analogy.story: You trust food with a clear date; unlabelled jars get thrown out.
analogy.breaks: Old doesn't always mean wrong (stable concepts), so combine age with feedback and code changes.

check.a: For example, last-updated date versus review interval, and negative reader feedback (also broken links and the lack of an owner).

documentation-as-a-platform-product.core: The most mature programmes treat documentation as a platform product: owners, a roadmap, templates, style guides, tooling (search, previews, linting), user research and metrics (usage, satisfaction, support-ticket deflection).

first_principles.problem: Docs are everyone's job and nobody's responsibility, so quality varies wildly.
truths: Templates and style guides raise consistency.
Good docs reduce support load measurably.
derivation: Assign **docs ownership** (platform docs team or writers).

analogy.title: Docs as a service with an SLA
analogy.story: Like any internal service, documentation has users, uptime (accuracy), support and improvements.
analogy.breaks: A central docs team can't write everything, so enable teams to self-serve good docs.

check.q: What is 'ticket deflection' in documentation metrics?
check.a: The reduction in support requests because users find answers in the docs themselves.
